title: Reserve Stock
readerIntent: Create, extend, consume, release, or expire a reservation safely.
priorKnowledge: Know trusted context, product/variant, requested quantity/unit, source, owner, and expiry policy.
summary: A reservation temporarily reduces available-to-sell under tenant-safe ownership, expiry, concurrency, and idempotency rules.

sections.heading: Flow
items: Resolve eligible sources and current availability.
Create reservation with stable owner/reference, source, quantity/unit, expiry, revision, and idempotency key.
Prevent oversell through atomic or qualified concurrency behavior.
Consume into allocation, release explicitly, or expire through governed job/event processing.
Persist evidence and invalidate affected availability cache after commit.

sections.heading: Business meaning
paragraphs: A reservation promises that eligible stock will be held temporarily for an owner such as a cart, order, quote, project, or service process. It reduces available-to-sell but does not prove fulfillment.
The owner, expiry, source, and quantity are explicit so abandoned holds can be released safely.

sections.heading: Concurrency control
items: Recalculate eligible availability at the authoritative source.
Acquire through qualified atomic or revision behavior.
Reject oversell and stale availability.
Use idempotency for repeated owner requests.
Return the existing reservation for an exact duplicate and reject conflict.

sections.heading: Example
paragraphs: A customer cart reserves 1.5 kilograms of produce for ten minutes from an eligible pool. Units validates the quantity. Inventory records the hold and updates availability.
Checkout consumes the hold into allocation. If checkout never completes, a governed scheduled job expires and releases it idempotently.

sections.heading: Lifecycle
items: Create, extend where policy permits, partially or fully consume, release, expire, cancel, and reconcile.
Do not extend beyond product, campaign, or fulfillment limits.
Do not release consumed quantity.
Treat late expiry and allocation races through revision policy.
Retain bounded audit evidence.

sections.heading: Tests and operations
items: Available, insufficient, exact-boundary, and fractional quantity.
Duplicate, conflicting, expired, released, and consumed reservation.
Concurrent requests and expiry/allocation race.
Wrong tenant, source, unit, owner, and permission.
Restart, repeated expiry job, unknown response, and reconciliation.
Reservation age, expiry backlog, conflict, and cache invalidation metrics.

sections.heading: Complete guide: How to reserve stock
paragraphs: A Stock Reservation protects units for a short-lived business process such as checkout, pickup preparation, or order allocation.

sections.heading: Business sequence
paragraphs: Reservations operate on Online operational Stock. Staged publishing remains appropriate for stable Warehouse, Pool, and Sourcing configuration, not live holds or movements.
Only authenticated modules and CronJob processes use these commands. Human BackOffice users act through an approved business API or workflow rather than calling internal reservation routes directly.
items: Sourcing identifies eligible Stock Pools and Warehouses.
Availability reports `ON_HAND`, `reservedQuantity`, and `AVAILABLE_TO_SELL`.
The checkout or order module requests a reservation with a unique idempotency key and expiry time.
Inventory atomically increases the balance's reserved quantity if enough stock remains.
Cancellation, release, or expiry returns the quantity to sale.
Fulfillment consumes the reservation and applies a matching Stock `ISSUE`; Inventory decreases on-hand and held quantity together.
